record.category: encyclopaedia corpus (monthly XML dumps, HTTP mirrors)

free_tier.stated: Complete public wiki dumps, monthly, free and anonymous. 'Downloads are also rate limited and capped at 3 connections per-IP.' The English Wikipedia article dump measured here is 25,800,511,704 bytes.
free_tier.notes: The dumps are being reorganised: the XML dumps are 'deprecated and will be sunset in January 2027' in favour of MediaWiki Content File Exports.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: one compressed file per dump. enwiki-latest-pages-articles.xml.bz2 is 25,800,511,704 bytes; ranged reads are supported (accept-ranges: bytes).

retention.stated: monthly snapshots are kept; 'latest' is replaced each run and older dated directories persist for a period the dump index does not quantify

egress.terms: Free, but conditioned on the User-Agent policy: 'If you are reading this on Wikimedia servers, please note that we are now enforcing the Wikimedia Foundation User-Agent Policy for dumps downloads. Downloads are also rate limited and capped at 3 connections per-IP ... Clients that do not respect the user-agent policy or who try to evade these limits may be blocked.'

record.interface_detail: HTTPS per file with Range support; rsync mirrors are listed on meta.wikimedia.org; the dump index at /backup-index.html gives every file with size and checksum.
record.tooling: curl/wget with a descriptive User-Agent, rsync against a mirror, and the checksum files that ship beside each dump.
record.chaining: A fixed encyclopaedia corpus to join against Common Crawl's web text; the 24 GiB article dump is small enough to hold beside a dataset snapshot, and the mirror list is the escape hatch when the per-IP cap binds.

limits.value: capped at 3 connections per IP, and rate limited; measured here at 1.661-2.617 MiB/s over one connection (three runs) and 2.647-7.649 MiB/s total over eight connections (three runs), so parallelism helped up to 3.6x and the cap did not refuse the eighth connection

record.limits_note: The User-Agent policy is enforced: a client without a descriptive agent may be blocked, and evasion attempts are named as a blocking reason on the front page.
record.binding_note: The documented 3-connection cap is a connection count, not a byte rate: eight parallel range reads all returned 206 and the best of them reached 7.649 MiB/s, which is about 645 GiB/day.

identity_cost.detail: No account and no key; a descriptive User-Agent is the only requirement, and it is not a credential.

record.reliability_note: The dump format is changing: XML dumps sunset in January 2027, so a pipeline built on pages-articles.xml has a dated migration to the Content File Exports format.
record.confidence_note: The file size came from a HEAD and the rate from a 64 MiB ranged read, three runs at each concurrency. All eight parallel requests returned 206, so the documented 3-connection cap did not refuse them at the transport level - whether it is enforced by rate, by UA or only at peak is not established.

evidence.proved: 'Downloads are also rate limited and capped at 3 connections per-IP', User-Agent policy enforcement, and the January 2027 XML sunset notice

64 MiB ranges at one connection: 2.617, 2.084 and 1.661 MiB/s across three runs, 206 with the range honoured; sha256 of the first range 3a74bf06ec319f7d702771523ec099593e7569f00b5bddfdbe3e76ddbc914ea7
eight parallel 206s totalling 2.647, 4.748 and 7.649 MiB/s against same-run one-connection baselines of 1.317, 2.918 and 2.337 MiB/s - parallelism helped, and no request was refused

record.notes: Caveat is the 2027 format change and the 3-connection rule. A single connection gives about 178 GiB/day at the mean, and the best eight-connection run reached 645 GiB/day - which the published cap says a client should not do. The whole English Wikipedia article dump is one day's single-connection allowance.

free_tier.stated: NO TOTAL QUOTA. Read verbatim from Commons:Maximum_file_size: 'there is no limit to the total size of uploads by an individual account.' Per-file cap is 5 GiB (5,368,709,120 bytes) via chunked upload, 100 MiB otherwise. Live API confirms: `maxuploadsize: 5368709120`.

egress.terms: free, unmetered, CDN (upload.wikimedia.org), no auth, Range supported. Wikimedia runs its own edge cache in front of Swift.

record.interface_detail: MediaWiki Action API + REST; `action=upload` with `stash`/`filekey` for chunked; `upload_by_url` right for server-side upload
record.tooling: mwclient / pywikibot / commons-cli; `upload` and `upload_by_url` are granted to the plain `user` group (verified in siteinfo usergroups), so a brand-new account can already do server-side upload without waiting
record.chaining: `upload_by_url` means Commons fetches the file from YOUR url. No local bandwidth at all. Files land at upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/<x>/<xy>/<name>, hash-addressed and immutably versioned.
record.limits_note: 5 GiB/file, 100 MiB without chunking; per-licence/scope review at the community level; thumbnailing capped at a 59 s timeout, 100 MP for GIFs

identity_cost.detail: Email. Account is username+password+email, no affiliation. Note the nuance: upload itself is in the base `user` group, but `reupload` (overwrite) needs autoconfirmed. So first uploads are open; overwriting an existing file needs account age.

record.reliability_note: The one platform here where a multi-TB batch is explicitly contemplated. Commons asks you to warn sysadmins before 'batch uploads amounting to several TB', which is an acknowledgement that people do it.

evidence.proved: same API with siprop=usergroups — `user` group holds ['upload','upload_by_url','reupload-own','move-categorypages']
'no limit to the total size of uploads by an individual account'; 5 GiB chunked / 100 MiB direct
149,839,243 files on the cluster (scale of the storage layer)
'Our swift backend storage is limited to files smaller than 5 Gb'

record.notes: NO TOTAL QUOTA. Read verbatim from Commons:Maximum_file_size: 'there is no limit to the total size of uploads by an individual account.' Per-file cap is 5 GiB (5,368,709,120 bytes) via chunked upload, 100 MiB otherwise. Live API confirms: `maxuploadsize: 5368709120`.
